text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliament passed amendments to the criminal code, allowing Defence Forces to conduct their own investigations on crimes among troops, but the Security Police will have the final say, parliamentary defence commission said.

- The barristers' college issued a statement protesting against State Court chairman Rait Maruste's strong position on a court decision to acquit lawyer Monika Magi who was accused of trying to bribe a judge. Justice Minister Paul Varul said court decisions that were not final should not be commented by high court officials.

- Nominated prime minister candidate Mart Siimann will today make a report to parliament (Riigikogu) on the principles for forming government. The Moderates and the right wing have announced they would remain in opposition and not support Siimann.

- The Estonian Embassy in Moscow said it had no previous information about a meeting of Jaak Saarniit, director of the Association of Large Enterprises, with the Russian foreign minister Yevgeny Primakov on Monday. Saarniit refuses to comment on the meeting.
- The Halle comet can be observed in Estonia until the end of April with the best period at Easter, scientists from the Tartu Observatory said.
- President Lennart Meri will leave on March 19 for a working visit to Japan, accompanied by a delegation of Estonian businessmen.
- Country-wide motor vehicle tax will come in force from next January, the government decided at its meeting on Tuesday.

- Rural parties in the governing coalition cannot decide whether to prefer Andres Varik or Avo Molder for agriculture minister. Chairman of the Country People's Party Arnold Ruutel said Varik would be better for the job.
- Estonian earth metal plant Silmet will get supplies of raw material from Uganda. Director of Silmet Priit Saksing signed a supply agreement for five years in Uganda last week.
- The Privatisation Agency will on Thursday announce a sale of a control-post of shares in the company Emex, accepting offers until May, officials said.
